articles.title: Karbi Anglong Peace Accord: Former Rebels Question Funds, Rehabilitation
articles.description: Former leaders of organisations that signed the Karbi Anglong Peace Accord have raised questions over the utilisation of funds released under the agreement and the political rehabilitation of former militants, five years after the pact was signed. The peace accord was signed on September 4, 2021, between the Centre, the Assam government and six Karbi Anglong-based armed groups, including the KLNLF, UPLA, PDCK and three factions of the KPLT. Under the agreement, the Centre and the state government had committed Rs 1,000 crore for various development projects in Karbi Anglong. While Rs 500 crore has been released so far, former leaders of the organisations alleged that they have not been able to ascertain how the amount was utilised. Speaking at a programme held to mark five years of the peace accord, former rebel leaders Jon Bey and Binod Timung alleged that the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council had misused a portion of the funds. They claimed that Rs 105 crore was spent on an eight-kilometre four-lane road connecting Gandhi Park in Diphu with the Assam University campus. The former leaders alleged that the road falls under the jurisdiction of the National Highways Authority of India ( NHAI ) and questioned why the project was undertaken without obtaining the required no-objection clearance. They also pointed out that the NHAI has subsequently invited a tender for the same road, raising questions over the earlier expenditure, they said. The leaders also questioned the reported expenditure of Rs 65 crore on a road project in Hamren, saying they were unaware of which road had been constructed using the funds. They claimed that the issues had been brought to the notice of Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma . Timung said another Rs 500 crore is expected to be utilised under the peace accord. Of this, Rs 209 crore would be spent on the construction of a session hall of the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, while Rs 290 crore would be used for the rehabilitation of former militants under the supervision of the Additional Director General of Police, he said. The former rebel leaders also expressed dissatisfaction over recent remarks by Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council Chief Executive Member Tuliram Ronghang regarding former militant leader Songbijit Ingti Kathar. Although Songbijit was not a signatory to the 2021 peace accord, the leaders said he was one of the prominent figures associated with the six organisations. Ronghang had reportedly said that the Centre was interested in holding discussions with Songbijit. The former rebel leaders criticised the statement and said it had caused resentment among the organisations that signed the accord. Songbijit is currently the Chief Executive Member of the Karbi Welfare Autonomous Council (KWAC), which was formed as part of the peace process, the leaders said. The former militants also raised concerns over political rehabilitation promised under the accord. Following the signing of the agreement, leaders and cadres of the participating organisations joined the BJP on October 9, 2021. The former leaders said 1,926 former militants had been assured political rehabilitation. However, they alleged that the promise had not been fulfilled adequately. At Friday's programme, the former rebel leaders said they would oppose the BJP in the 2027 Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council elections if the party does not provide tickets to leaders nominated by the organisations that signed the peace accord. articles.title: Odisha plans 129km outer ring road to ease traffic; link Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Puri and Khordha
articles.description: The Odisha government on Saturday announced a major infrastructure plan to ease traffic congestion in and around Bhubaneswar, with work on the proposed Outer Ring Road expected to begin soon. The alignment of the project was finalised at a meeting held on Saturday under the chairmanship of the Works Minister Prithiviraj Harichandan. According to the plan, the proposed Outer Ring Road will be integrated with the Capital Region Ring Road to create a wider road network around the Bhubaneswar-Cuttack urban region. The Outer Ring Road will stretch for around 129 km, while the Capital Region Ring Road will add another 90 km to the overall connectivity network. Encompassing Cuttack, BBSR, Puri, Khorda One end of the Outer Ring Road is proposed to touch Baghamari, while the other will extend beyond Choudwar Municipality. The corridor will encompass areas including Cuttack, Bhubaneswar, Puri, Pipili, Khordha Municipality and Choudwar Municipality. The project is expected to help divert through-traffic away from congested urban stretches and provide smoother connectivity between key locations in the Capital Region. Apart from the ring road project, the government has also decided to move ahead with the tender process for an elevated road from Kalinga Studio Square to Nuagaon. A separate road project connecting Raghunathpur with Trisulia has also been planned, with the tender process set to be initiated. Foundation In October The Works Minister said the foundation stone for the projects is likely to be laid before the first week of October. Once implemented, the proposed road network is expected to significantly improve connectivity between Bhubaneswar and adjoining urban areas while reducing pressure on existing city roads and major traffic corridors. The projects form part of the State government’s broader plan to strengthen transport infrastructure and address increasing vehicular congestion across the rapidly expanding Capital Region.

articles.title: Government e-Marketplace (GeM) Signs MoU to Boost Recycled and Upcycled Textiles Procurement
articles.description: It is an interesting development by the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) to take an important step to foster sustainable public procurement with the signing of an MoU, which will boost the use of recycled and upcycled textile goods through procurement. This is an important development since public procurement has the potential to generate huge demand for sustainable goods. By promoting the use of recycled and upcycled textile goods in the purchase process through GeM, a big market for such items can be generated.
